measures: what a client sees: cached latency, and generating latency for the configured provider
provider: ollama/llama3.1:8b (Q4_K_M, 4.9GB) on localhost via host.docker.internal — LOCAL inference, not a hosted provider
model_rationale: 8B is what a real self-hosted deployment runs. llama3.2 (3.2B) was measured first and is not a production self-hosting choice; it makes the cold path look cheaper than any deployment would experience. 70B was checked and skipped: Q4 needs roughly 40GB against 18GB physical on this machine, so it would swap and time paging rather than inference. Chosen for realism, not because it produces a larger number.
does_not_measure: the README's '12.5s avg (GPT-4o / Claude)'. The cold figure describes whichever provider this gateway is configured with, recorded under 'provider' below.
any hosted provider unless 'provider' says so — check it before quoting the cold number or the speedup
cached_paths_are_not_one_number: exact and semantic are reported separately and never averaged. Exact can return before the query is embedded; semantic cannot. An average over them is set by the traffic mix, not by the cache.
speedup_condition: ratio of the two measured means above; inherits the cold path's provider condition entirely
